   841	9.2 Faction Rules and Abilities
   842	9.2.1     Crafting. The Vagabond can exhaust H to activate
   843	its pawn as a crafting piece, ignoring the once-per-
   844	turn limit (4.1.1). If the Vagabond crafts an item,
   845	he may immediately take it, face up.

   847	rior (so he cannot rule a clearing or stop another player
   848	from ruling one). The Vagabond pawn cannot be
   849	removed from the map.
   850	I     Full Removal. Whenever an enemy player uses
   851	an effect that says it removes all enemy pieces
   852	from a clearing (such as Alliance revolts, Favor of
   853	the Mice cards, Conspiracy bombs) with the Vaga­
   854	bond, the Vagabond damages three items.

   856	who rules his origin or destination clearing (4.2.1).

   858	is defenseless (4.3.5.II) if he has no undamaged S.

   860	items he acquires. Instead of a Crafted Items box,
   861	he has a Satchel and various item tracks. Items on
   862	the Vagabond’s faction board can be face up or
   863	face down. The Vagabond exhausts face-up un­
   864	damaged items, flipping them face down, to take
   865	many actions.

   867	in your Satchel, place it in an empty matching
   868	track space if able. If a T, X, or B on a track
   869	is flipped face down, place it in your Satchel.

   875	aged S, face up or face down, in his Satchel.

   883	victory condition (3.3.1). Instead, in games with

   885	dominance card to form a coalition with another
   886	player, placing his score marker on that player’s
   887	faction board. (The Vagabond no longer scores points.)
   888	That player must have fewer victory points than
   889	each other player except the Vagabond forming
   890	the coalition, and that player cannot be in a coa­
   891	lition. If there is a tie for fewest victory points, he
   892	chooses one tied player. If the coalitioned player
   893	wins the game, the Vagabond also wins.

   895	tionships chart, which has four spaces on the Al­

   897	ship marker for each non-Vagabond faction.
